pass_b_english: The desolate state of the land is a result of its complete abandonment, for it is known that the nations of the Saracens, as well as the Assyrians, and even the innermost desert, are referred to as Arabs, given their proximity to the Arabs.
It is likely that the Saracens from Arabia also roam around the deserts of the Assyrians.
Wild beasts will rest there, and the houses will be filled with sound (Isaiah 13:21-22).
This means that the houses will have no inhabitants, and instead, they will be filled with the sounds of desolation.
Demons are said to haunt desolate places, making them their dwelling, and it is there that they will dance.
Sirens, which are birds known for their beautiful singing, or possibly owls, according to the Hebrew translation, will also rest in these deserted areas.
The wild donkeys are referred to as centaurs, and hedgehogs with sharp thorns are likened to frightened mice.
All these creatures are naturally drawn to deserted cities or houses.
The descents into these areas are automatic and planned, almost as if they were discovered by the very fact of what has happened.
In the deserts and silent places, a faint echo can be heard, which seems to emanate from the great silence, and this sound is disturbing, entering the ears of those who are resting.
As a result, wild beasts will rest in these areas, and the houses will be filled with sound, having no human inhabitants.
Demons will dance there, as they are known to haunt desolate places and make them their dwelling.
The presence of centaurs and hedgehogs with sharp thorns, which are like frightened mice, is also characteristic of these deserted areas.
All these elements are fitting for deserted cities or houses, and it is said that this state will come quickly, without delay.

This desolation may bring bitter worry to the Assyrians or a notable calling to the Israelites, for when they were in captivity, they thought they would be freed when the Persians and Medes, along with the Babylonians, campaigned.
In this context, a promise is made to the Israelites that they will experience a swift release from their troubles, and that their prayers will not be delayed, but will be answered quickly.
The Lord will have mercy on Jacob and choose Israel again, and they will rest on their land, with strangers being added to them.
Nations will take them and bring them to their place, and they will inherit and multiply on the land of God, serving as slaves and slave women.
Those who took them captive will be captives, and those who ruled over them will be ruled over, and this will occur on that day.
